note.p: This is a long-shot, but the name is unusual, corresponding to a district near Edinburgh, but there are no entries in the ODNB. In 1785 (with another edition in 1787)a Hercules Cramond published Outlines of Human Life aged 30 in London, and in 1789 Hercules and Robert Cramond published a Letter to the National Assembly. A Hercules Crammond was buried in Greyfriars, kirkyard, Edinburgh in Feb 1784. The author, Hercules, identifies his father as Robert Cramond, b. 1703 in Edinburgh. but says his unccle was a Scottish sea-farer who lived past the meridian of life. There is a single m in the author's name and a double m on the grave report, but such variation is not uncommon.

It seems likely that one of Hercules and Robert were visiting London and sought out Godwin, on philosophiccal grounds. Hercules would have been a similar age to Godwin. Robert might be a son but it was also the name of his brother.
